item.title: How 3000+ donors came together to raise $1.1 million for the Naroditsky Fund
item.description: Daniel Naroditsky touched millions as a player, commentator, and teacher. After his untimely passing, many who had never met him felt they had lost someone close. In the months that followed, the chess community came together and raised $1.1 million to establish the Naroditsky Memorial and Fellowship Fund. Here is the story behind the initiative and how it is carrying Daniel's legacy into the future. Photo: ChessBase

item.title: 59th Biel Chess Festival 2026: Everything You Need to Know
item.description: The grueling, thrilling, and unique marathon of elite chess is back. The 59th Biel International Chess Festival is set to take over the Biel Congress Center (Kongresshaus) in Switzerland from July 11 to 24, 2026. For over half a century, Biel has been a sacred ground for chess players. What makes it truly special is its signature Triathlon format, a brutal test of versatility where players must fight across Classical, Rapid, and Blitz disciplines to claim the ultimate crown.

item.title: India to Host the Asian Junior Open & Girls Chess Championships 2026 in Mumbai
item.description: The All India Chess Federation, under the aegis of the Asian Chess Federation and FIDE, is proud to host the Asian Junior Open & Girls Chess Championships 2026. This premier continental event will bring together Asia’s brightest young talents to compete at the prestigious ITC Maratha in Mumbai from August 16th to 26th, 2026

item.title: Alireza Firouzja Wins Thrilling Super Rapid and Blitz Croatia 2026 in Armageddon Playoff
item.description: Alireza Firouzja won Super Chess Rapid and Blitz Croatia 2026. What originally looked like a comfortable Sunday cruise for Alireza Firouzja transformed into one of the most nerve-wracking, volatile final days in the history of the tour, culminating in the first-ever GCT title decided by an Armageddon playoff. Alireza drew against Nodirbek Abdusattorov in Armageddon to win Super Chess Rapid and Blitz Croatia. Photo: Lennart Ootes

item.title: Kunte Kaka would be smiling from heaven!
item.description: On 8th July 2026, at the first-ever Pune International GM Round Robin, 18-year-old Aswath S won on demand in the final round to become India's 98th Grandmaster, while Pune's young FM Advik Agrawal secured an IM norm. The tournament was the lifelong dream of Prakash Kunte - the beloved "Kunte Kaka" - who passed away just a day before its conclusion, while his son GM Abhijit Kunte brought his vision to life.

item.title: Beyond the 64 Squares: How Chess is Transforming Lives Behind the Scenes at Premier Chess Academy
item.description: When we talk about chess changing lives, we often visualize a young prodigy from a humble background rising through the ranks to claim a Grandmaster title. We think of the intense battles on the chessboard, the rating spikes, and the tournament podiums. But there is an entirely different, equally powerful revolution happening away from the spotlight. Behind the screens of online training platforms, a quiet transformation is unfolding in the lives of the coaches, administrators, and support staff who dedicate themselves to the royal game.

item.title: Rudra Pratap and Liyaa Krishnan are 2026 Under-7 National Champions
item.description: Rudra Pratap from Bihar scored 8/9 points to win the 39th National Under-7 Open Chess Championship. Rudra scored a perfect 8/8, and then he lost the final round, but better tiebreaks helped him clinch the title. In the Under-7 Girls group, Ns Liyaa Krishnan of Maharashtra scored a perfect 9/9 to win the National Championship with a clear 1.5 point lead. The tournament was organised in Nagpur from 30th June to 4th July 2026. The total prize fund was ₹5,00,000 with top 3 prizes of ₹50,000, ₹36,000, and ₹30,000 in both groups. Photo: Ayush Jain

item.title: What your chess instinct is trying to tell you
item.description: What if the first move you notice says more about you than it does about the position? Chess is much more than calculation. It's a reflection of how your mind has been shaped over the years. Every player has a different instinct, influenced by their experiences, strengths, and even their most recent games. These patterns shape the way we see the board. Let's explore what your first instinct reveals. Image is AI generated.

item.title: Divi Bijesh, Sarbartho Mani, Saiaastha Singh and Sattwik Swain, Shines at FIDE World Cup Cadets 2026
item.description: Four talented Indian youngsters excelled at the FIDE World Cup Cadets 2026, securing four medals for the country. Divi Bijesh clinched back-to-back gold medals in consecutive editions. She scored 9/11 points to win the gold medal in Under-12 Girls. In the Under-10 Open, two Indian players secured podium finishes. Sarbartho Mani and Sattwin Swain scored 8.5/11 to finish in 2nd and 3rd place, respectively. In the Under-8 Girls, Saiaastha Singh secured the Bronze Medal after scoring 8.5/11 points. Photos: IM Abhishek Kelkar

item.title: 21st Malaysian Chess Festival 2026: A Guide for Players & Fans
item.description: Come every August and September, the regional chess spotlight falls on Malaysia. That is when players from around the country and overseas converge on Kuala Lumpur for what has become one of the region's best-loved annual gatherings, the Malaysian Chess Festival. This year marks the 21st Malaysian Chess Festival, which will be held from 28th August to 6th September 2026 at KL Gateway Mall in Kuala Lumpur. Over ten days, the venue will once again be transformed into a bustle of activity as players of all ages and abilities battle over the chessboard, renewing friendships while creating new memories.

item.title: The Man Who Keeps the Peace: Vasant BH on Two Decades of Arbitering
item.description: International Arbiter Vasant BH is a familiar face at Indian chess tournaments from the Delhi Open to major international events, including a stint officiating at the World Cup in Goa in 2025. But his journey into arbitering wasn't planned. It began, quite simply, because of his son. In this candid conversation, Vasant BH looks back at nearly two decades on the tournament floor, the disputes, the dilemmas, the emotional moments, and the lessons he's picked up along the way.

item.title: Arvind Iyer Wins 1st Unicorn International Open Fide Rapid Rating 2026
item.description: Arvind Iyer scored 8/9 points in the 1st Unicorn International Open Fide Rapid Rating Chess Tournament 2026. Arvind Iyer, IM Srijit Paul, Indrajeet Mahindrakar, and Kamad Mishra scored 8/9 points to finish in 1st to 4th places, respectively, according to tiebreak scores. Unicorn Chess Academy organised the tournament from 28th to 29th June 2026 in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. The total prize fund was ₹2,00,000, with the top 3 prizes being ₹30,000, ₹25,000, and ₹20,000. Photos: Aditi Shrivastava

item.title: Nihal Sarin on Winning the Bullet Chess Championship 2026
item.description: Nihal Sarin's Bullet Chess Championship 2026 triumph was one of the most remarkable performances of his career. After defeating some of the world's fastest players, he capped it off by beating Alireza Firouzja 15 games in a row in the final. In a recent conversation with IM Sagar Shah, Nihal spoke about his mindset and the subtle skills that define bullet chess, his friendship with the late GM Daniel Naroditsky and much more. Read the full interview to discover the story behind one of the greatest bullet performances ever.

item.title: Bangalore Chess Club raises Rs. 61,200 to support chess players
item.description: On 25th January 2026, as part of its Republic Day special, Bangalore Chess Club hosted the second edition of its annual fundraiser rapid tournament, bringing together over 200 chess enthusiasts from across the city. The event raised an impressive Rs. 61,200 and donated it towards the HelpChess Foundation to support chess players. Read the article to know how the Bangalore Chess Club is promoting chess in Bangalore.

item.title: Alireza Firouzja Dominates on the 2nd Day of Super Rapid Croatia 2026
item.description: Alireza Firouzja is maintaining his great form at Super Rapid Croatia 2026. After getting an early lead on day 1, he repeated the same performance once again and scored 5/6 points on day 2. Alireza is leading the tournament with 10/12 points, while 4 players are in joint 2nd place with 7/12 points. World Champion D Gukesh started his day with a loss against Bogdan Daniel Deac, but then he scored 2 consecutive wins over Jorden van Foreest and Anish Giri, which took him to the joint 2nd place. Photo: Lennart Ootes
